Introduction to Dataset¶¶

Dataset Name: Global Environmental Trends 2020-2024¶

Source: OpenML

The dataset was Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/adilshamim8/temperature/data)

This dataset offers a detailed breakdown of critical environmental indicators obtained from several nations over 24 years (2000–2024). It is intended to assist with analyses that investigate how human activity, environmental changes, and climate variables interact.

Data Wrangling¶

In [105]:
df_grouped = df.groupby(["Year", "Country"]).agg({"Avg_Temperature_degC" : 'mean',
                                                      "CO2_Emissions_tons_per_capita" : 'mean',
                                                      "Sea_Level_Rise_mm" : 'max',
                                                      "Rainfall_mm" : 'max',
                                                      "Population" : 'mean',
                                                      "Renewable_Energy_pct" : 'mean',
                                                      "Extreme_Weather_Events" : 'max',
                                                      "Forest_Area_pct" : 'mean'})
df_new = df_grouped.copy()
df_new['Abv_Avg_Events'] = (df_new['Extreme_Weather_Events'] >= df_new['Extreme_Weather_Events'].median()).astype(int)

def climate(temp):
    if temp >= 25:
        return "Warm"
    elif temp >= 10:
        return "Temperate"
    else:
        return "Cold"
df_new['Climate'] = df_new['Avg_Temperature_degC'].apply(climate)
df_new.to_csv("cleanedtemperature2.csv")

2. Bar chart for Top 10 Most Frequent Countries¶

In [89]:
top_countries = df['Country'].value_counts().nlargest(10).reset_index()
top_countries.columns = ['Country', 'Frequency']

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(
    data=top_countries,
    x='Frequency',
    y='Country',
    hue='Frequency',        # Required to use palette without warning
    palette='viridis',
    dodge=False,
    legend=False            # Hides redundant legend
)
plt.title('Top 10 Most Frequent Countries in Dataset')
plt.xlabel('Frequency')
plt.ylabel('Country')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Countplot: Distribution of Extreme Weather Events¶

In [91]:
# Create the countplot
ax = sns.countplot(
    data=df,
    x='Extreme_Weather_Events',
    hue='Extreme_Weather_Events',
    palette='coolwarm',
    legend=False
)

# Set title and axis labels
plt.title('Distribution of Extreme Weather Events', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Number of Extreme Weather Events', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=12)

# Add annotations on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    ax.annotate(f'{height}', 
                (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height), 
                ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Interpretation (can also be shown as plt.text inside plot if needed)
# For now, print it below for clarity:
event_counts = df['Extreme_Weather_Events'].value_counts().sort_index()
most_common = event_counts.idxmax()
least_common = event_counts.idxmin()

print(f" Interpretation: The plot shows that {most_common} extreme weather events occurred most frequently in the dataset.")
print(f"The least common number of events recorded is {least_common}.")

 Interpretation: The plot shows that 8 extreme weather events occurred most frequently in the dataset.
The least common number of events recorded is 4.

Lineplot: Average Number of Extreme Events Per Year¶

In [93]:
# Group by Year and calculate the average number of extreme weather events per year
df_avg_events_per_year = df.groupby('Year')['Extreme_Weather_Events'].mean().reset_index()

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
sns.lineplot(data=df_avg_events_per_year, x='Year', y='Extreme_Weather_Events', marker='o', color='darkred')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Average Number of Extreme Weather Events Per Year', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Average Number of Events', fontsize=12)
plt.tight_layout()

# Show plot
plt.show()

CO2 Emissions per Capita Over Time Plot¶

In [95]:
# Focus on five selected countries
selected_countries = [ "China", "USA","Brazil"]
df_filtered = df[df["Country"].isin(selected_countries)]

# Set up plot style
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create the line plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
for country in selected_countries:
    country_data = df_filtered[df_filtered["Country"] == country]
    plt.plot(
        country_data["Year"],
        country_data["CO2_Emissions_tons_per_capita"],
        label=country
    )

# Chart formatting
plt.title("CO2 Emissions per Capita Over Time (2000–2023)", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("CO2 Emissions (tons per capita)")
plt.legend(title="Country")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Lineplot: Average Temperature Trends for Selected Countries¶

In [97]:
# List of selected countries
selected_countries = ['USA', 'India','Australia', 'Brazil', 'China']

# Filter dataset for those countries
df_selected = df[df['Country'].isin(selected_countries)]

# Group by Year and Country, compute mean temperature per year
df_grouped = df_selected.groupby(['Year', 'Country'])['Avg_Temperature_degC'].mean().reset_index()

# Plot setup
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Loop to plot each country's line
for country in selected_countries:
    country_data = df_grouped[df_grouped['Country'] == country]
    sns.lineplot(data=country_data, x='Year', y='Avg_Temperature_degC', label=country)

# Plot aesthetics
plt.title('Average Temperature Trends (Selected Countries)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Year')
plt.ylabel('Average Temperature (°C)')
plt.legend(title='Country')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file (change the path as needed)
plt.savefig('temperature_trends.png', format='png')  # Saves the plot as a PNG file

# Show plot
plt.show()

Lineplot: CO2 Emissions Over Time for Top 5 Emitting Countries¶

In [99]:
top_countries = df.groupby('Country')['CO2_Emissions_tons_per_capita'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(5).index
subset = df[df['Country'].isin(top_countries)]

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.lineplot(data=subset, x='Year', y='CO2_Emissions_tons_per_capita', hue='Country', marker='o')
plt.title('CO2 Emissions Over Time for Top 5 Emitting Countries', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Year')
plt.ylabel('CO2 Emissions (tons per capita)')
plt.legend(title='Country')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("Interpretation:")
print("This line plot shows how CO2 emissions per capita have evolved over time for the top 5 countries.")
print("Some show steady growth, while others show a decline or stabilization, possibly due to policy changes or technology.")

Interpretation:
This line plot shows how CO2 emissions per capita have evolved over time for the top 5 countries.
Some show steady growth, while others show a decline or stabilization, possibly due to policy changes or technology.
